### [Preparing for the 2026 US midterms](https://www.anthropic.com/news/2026-us-midterms)

**Anthropic** · 2026-10-14

Anthropic updated its election safeguards for the 2026 US midterms, incorporating state-specific Democracy Works voting data and live election night results directly into Claude.ai conversations.

- Analysis of 250,000 US Claude.ai conversations showed 5.75% involved politics/policy, 0.51% involved elections, 0.01% asked for voting recommendations, and 0.002% violated election integrity policies.
- Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5 achieved a 99% score on Anthropic's internal political evenhandedness evaluation.
- Claude.ai will integrate Democracy Works data directly into responses for state-specific voting instructions and will display real-time official vote counts on election night.
- Independent evaluations of Claude's handling of contentious topics and free expression were conducted by organizations including The Future of Free Speech and the Foundation for American Innovation.

**Why it matters:** The updates allow users to receive real-time, nonpartisan election results and localized voting instructions directly within the chat interface while reducing model refusals on political topics.

### [Deno is joining Cloudflare](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Oct/9/deno-is-joining-cloudflare/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-10-09

Cloudflare is acquiring Deno to advance self-hostable Workers via celld, while sunsetting official Deno runtime development after one year of maintenance.

- Cloudflare is acquiring Deno to use its celld implementation to make self-hosting workerd a first-class supported model for Cloudflare Workers apps.
- Cloudflare will support the Deno runtime for one year with monthly bug fixes and security updates before ending active development, leaving it open source for community takeover.
- Creator Ryan Dahl cited Deno's shift toward complete Node.js compatibility as a reason for ending development, noting marginal security, UX, and performance gains over Node do not solve big problems.
- celld provides a new server development model using Durable Objects patterns that depend solely on object storage for persistence and coordination.
- While Node.js stabilized its own permissions system in v22.13.0, it still lacks Deno's capability to allow-list specific network hosts.

**Why it matters:** The acquisition shifts focus toward object-storage-backed stateful server architectures while effectively ending official corporate backing for Deno as a standalone Node.js alternative.

`deno` `cloudflare` `javascript` `serverless` `nodejs`
